s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest and back pain with electrocardiogram changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers, suggesting an acute cardiac syndrome
salient_findings: Persistent chest and back pain
Diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
Cystic mass above the left atrium on contrast-enhanced CT scan
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
History of hypertension
Chest discomfort and dyspnea on exertion for two months
Sinus rhythm with occasional premature ventricular complexes on electrocardiogram
Elevated cardiac troponin I level of 620 pg/mL
Diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle on transthoracic echocardiography
Cystic mass above the left atrium on contrast-enhanced CT scan
Mass had heterogeneous attenuation (15–56 Hounsfield units) on noncontrast images
Mass exhibited slight contrast enhancement
Transient cardiogenic shock that responded to noradrenaline support

shortlist.label: Cardiac tamponade
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass above the left atrium and transient cardiogenic shock

shortlist.label: Pericardial cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass above the left atrium with heterogeneous attenuation and slight contrast enhancement

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac troponin I level and diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle

shortlist.label: Cardiac metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass above the left atrium and history of hypertension, which may increase the risk of cardiac metastasis

shortlist.label: Left atrial myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic mass above the left atrium and potential for obstructive shock

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with chest discomfort, dyspnea on exertion, and transient cardiogenic shock, along with the finding of a large cystic mass above the left atrium that could be compressing the heart, is most consistent with cardiac tamponade. The elevated cardiac troponin I level and diffuse hypokinesis of the left ventricle also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pericardial cyst
rejected.why: While the mass could be a pericardial cyst, the patient's symptoms and the mass's effect on cardiac function are more suggestive of tamponade.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: The electrocardiogram shows diffuse ST-segment depression and ST elevation in lead aVR, but the presence of a large cystic mass above the left atrium is not typical for myocardial infarction.

rejected.label: Cardiac metastasis
rejected.why: There is no mention of a primary cancer, and the mass's characteristics are not specifically suggestive of metastasis.

rejected.label: Left atrial myxoma
rejected.why: The mass is located above the left atrium, not within it, making left atrial myxoma less likely.
